title: Microsoft Purview DLP: policy sync status within 30 minutes (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned faster sync, automatic enablement and rollout windows, while preserving the different timings still published on Learn. The device-status path, Graph query and Endpoint DLP licensing are supported; minor corrections concern a missing audit-mode citation and a checklist instruction to change a policy that has no controls-table row.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Per-device Endpoint DLP policy sync status is available at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices.

claims.claim: Policy sync status reports whether an onboarded device received the latest policy version.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.

claims.claim: Updated means the device is up to date with current policy versions.
claims.quote: Device is up to date with the current versions of policies.

claims.claim: Not updated is a policy sync status indicating the device has not synced the latest policy updates.
claims.quote: This device isn't synced the latest policy updates.

claims.claim: Not available is the third possible policy sync status.
claims.quote: Configuration status and the Policy sync status of all your onboarded devices have three possible values. Updated; Not updated; Not available.

claims.claim: The faster SLA does not change the policy sync status values' meaning.
claims.quote: This change improves the timing of DLP policy enforcement but does not change policy behavior, data processing, or data storage.

claims.claim: Devices must be online to receive policy updates, so offline devices cannot sync new policies.
claims.quote: Devices must be online for the policy update to happen. If the status isn't updating, check the last time the device was seen.

claims.claim: The device details pane provides remediation guidance when policy sync status remains Not updated.
claims.quote: If the status is Not updated or Not available, follow the remediation steps in the details pane and the steps in the workflow diagram.

claims.where: controls[0].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery is the documented read-only Graph operation for querying advanced hunting data.
claims.quote: Queries a specified set of event, activity, or entity data supported by Microsoft 365 Defender. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery

claims.claim: The Graph request body uses the Query property.
claims.quote: In the request body, provide a JSON object with the Query property, and optionally include the Timespan and workspaceId properties.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo's DlpInfo column provides Endpoint DLP device information corresponding to the portal's device status data.
claims.quote: The JSON object can be used to query and report on device configuration status, policy synchronization status, Endpoint DLP enablement, and other configuration details for onboarded devices. These values correspond to the device information available in the DLP device onboarding page.

claims.claim: The interactive advanced hunting route is in the Microsoft Defender portal.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft Defender portal. Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting. Query the DeviceInfo table.

claims.claim: The Graph hunting call requires the permissions listed in its reference.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account): ThreatHunting.Read.All; higher privileged: ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All. Application: ThreatHunting.Read.All; higher privileged: ThreatHunting.ReadWrite.All.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; controls[1].note; rendered controls table
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no UI or API switch to opt out of faster policy sync in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP faster policy sync 30 minutes opt out disable setting Set-DlpCompliancePolicy. Read MC1317834, sync troubleshooting and Set-DlpCompliancePolicy search excerpts; policy disabling is documented, but no faster-sync opt-out found.

claims.claim: The checklist instructs the reader to change an Endpoint DLP policy in a pilot scope, but the controls table has no policy-editing control.
claims.quote: Change one Endpoint DLP policy in a pilot scope and note how long Policy sync status takes to show Updated for a test device. Table rows: Per-device policy sync status for Endpoint DLP; Switch to opt out of the faster policy sync.
claims.fix: Replace the At rollout policy-change bullet with 'Observe Policy sync status for an onboarded test device after a planned policy change and note how long it takes to show Updated.' This keeps the instruction on the documented status row without adding a control.

claims.claim: DLP policy changes can be tested in simulation mode before enforcement.
claims.quote: When you deploy a new policy or need to modify an existing one, you should run it in simulation mode, and then review the alerts to assess its accuracy.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP supports audit-only testing of policy behaviour.
claims.quote: This scenario shows how to create a Microsoft Purview DLP policy using the U.S. PII Data Enhanced template to monitor sensitive data on endpoint devices. The policy runs in audit-only (simulation) mode
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-create-policy-audit-activities to sources for the audit-mode advice.

claims.claim: MC1317834 recommends optionally informing security and compliance teams that DLP changes will take effect more quickly.
claims.quote: Optionally, inform security and compliance teams that DLP changes will take effect more quickly to support faster response expectations.

claims.claim: Viewing per-device policy sync status is read-only observation, not a control that speeds up or delays enforcement.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device. Select a device to open the details pane for more information on the policy sync status.

claims.claim: The notice describes a timing improvement rather than a new automated policy action.
claims.quote: This change improves the timing of DLP policy enforcement but does not change policy behavior, data processing, or data storage.
